content.content:
60	
61	*The breaker (the Pillar 3 price).* On the home-ship you close a breaker (V3, a tap). No hold, no confirm: the inrush flickers the corridor lamps (`INRUSH_PM`, `INRUSH_STEPS`, cited from the Graph) and the web saw that. The cost of the experiment is the inrush itself, not a dialog.
62	
63	*Co-op beats* — a crewmate already at the object as the visible reason for `BUSY`, the revive channel on a downed crewmate, the friendly-harm act — are Vertical Slice B. The MVP fantasy rests on your own hands.
64	
65	**Pillar quotes the section carries.** Pillar 4, verbatim: "No lie is unfalsifiable: the truth is always available through the physical world, a second instrument, a saner crewmate, the human channel, or time — and checking costs time, risk or trust." The deferred outcome (IA-12) is that sentence made into a mechanic: the check is *time* (the full bar), *risk* (standing still, lit, noisy) and never free. Pillar 3: "The players' light, noise, power use and restraint raise or lower its attention… Restraint and stealth are real strategies" — every channel is lit, stationary and noisy; restraint means choosing which jobs to do. Pillar 1: "A pipe may *look* fixed, but the room still gets cold, the air still thins, the pressure still drops" — every verb's result is a consequence-channel change; Interaction writes none of it itself (Failure & Trail, row 15: "no data crosses"). Pillar 2: "Every breach is preceded by a tell a careful player could have perceived" — the player's own verbs are exogenous (LS-13) and carry their own tell (a severed stub's hiss, the inrush flicker), and a verb never outruns a tell because movement always cancels. Pillar 5: "losing the home-ship or a crewmate costs ship and body, never knowledge" — a patch is free but decays, a FULL repair costs a part that comes from deeper, and nothing a verb teaches is lost on death (restart from the last autosave, Save/Load SL-7).
66	
67	**Design tests.** *Primary:* when a choice makes an action cheaper to do than to be sure of, make the checking cheaper than the lie, never free; when a prompt could be drawn where `lit(ref)` is false, never draw it — a prompt must not lie by omission. *Subordinate:* (1) **"I can leave now" (P2)** — when a verb could hold the player in place versus let any move release them, release them; fails if any verb, at any sanity, rhythm or Attention level, holds the body. (2) **The prompt never answers (P4)** — when a prompt, cue or rejection could reveal module-body truth at zero time, risk or trust versus only after the full channel, after the channel; fails if a player can learn a pipe's real state by tapping and releasing, or by pressing a FULL repair, cancelling at any tick and reading the part stock, the weight cue or the reserved bucket. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: and by a one-block PATCH tap-and-cancel, whose Graph state, descriptors and noise are identical at hp 10000, 5999, 5000 and 4000 with `hp_cap` 10000, because the PATCH guard of IA-17 makes no M7 call there; AC-IA-26.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: from the first credited block on, a cancel, abort or restore consumes the part in both truth branches, so believing a lie and acting on it costs a part, which is honest under P4; only a channel that runs to its end may return the part, IA-18.)* (3) **No stat penalties from interactions (P4 secondary)** — a −10 % repair speed at low sanity versus a false gauge: the false gauge; channel durations are fixed per verb and read no sanity, Attention, rhythm or device. (4) **The hands work only in the light (P3)** — act without light versus require light: require light; exactly three listed object exceptions (actor verbs, `throw_glowstick` and the self-patch, have no object to light, IA-6) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. (5) **Physical answer, not message (P1)** — a "repaired!" toast versus the hiss stopping: the hiss; completion is a cue, the result is the world.
68	
69	**How the fantasy deepens under hallucination — and must not break.** The rule of the section: *the prompt never answers; the work does.* Prompt existence is a function of the object's declared kind, the tool in hand, `lit` and `in_reach` only (IA-11), so the prompt says the same thing to a sane and to a hallucinating player. What hallucination changes is what the player *believes before* reaching, and the work is how they find out.
70	- **A hallucinated-broken, truly healthy pipe (false system state):** the sprite and gauge read broken. The prompt appears (it is kind-based); the bar runs the full 180 ticks, pixel- and sound-identical to a real patch; the Graph receives zero mutator calls; the job resolves `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)` and the *nothing happened* cue. "Three seconds of noise for nothing — it wasn't broken. My eyes are going." The check cost time, noise and light; it was never free.
71	- **A hallucinated-fixed, truly leaking pipe (hp 2000):** looks whole, gauge green. The prompt still appears; if the player patches anyway, the real increments land against 2000. The cold is the truth (P1): the cautious player who patches a "fixed" pipe is rewarded by physics, not by a message.
72	- **A phantom entity:** no subject, so never lit, never focused, never prompted; `interact` with no focus is a no-op with no command and no pre-play; the only sound is the Adapter's local `cue_input_ignored`, identical for every no-focus press, so it tells a phantom from empty space no better than silence *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: conformed to IA-4 and the Controller's ignored-input cue)*. **A claim correction the section must carry:** reaching for a thing falsifies *objects*, not monsters — real HORROR subjects also take no verb at MVP, so a missing prompt is not evidence about a monster either way (true at MVP; in Vertical Slice B IA-31's precondition keeps the plate from discriminating real horrors from crewmates drawn as horrors). That symmetry is by design; the truth about monsters lives in the footprint of the world (sound, frost, hull stress), not in the hands.
73	- **Phantom salvage (a real registered `junk_` item):** every verb works normally, because it is a real item. The truth is the weight cue (Suit), the scanner field check (`FIELD_CHECK_TICKS`, scanner in hand) or the trip home — the cheaper check that Pillar 4(d) requires.
74	- **A crewmate rendered as a horror (Vertical Slice B):** for an actor whose Sanity level is below the harm threshold the prompt reads the equipped tool's ordinary verb (`E · Cut`), never a target noun; a sane actor gets no prompt and a forced attempt is rejected `NOT_ELIGIBLE`. The horror is that the hands work. (Two rulings travel with this bullet. IA-31's **blocking Vertical Slice B precondition**: the plate must not tell a crewmate drawn as a horror from a real horror, so real horrors carry a `repel` declaration with the same `verb_name_key` and the eligibility bit is the class-(c) render level. And the **self-knowledge ruling**: the plate's presence is honest knowledge of the actor's *own* sanity, which Pillar 4 allows.)
75	
76	**Reference techniques — adopt / reject.**
77	
78	| Reference | Technique | Verdict | Why |
79	|---|---|---|---|
80	| Project Zomboid | Timed contextual actions on a linear bar, cancelled by moving; no skill-check minigame | **Adopt** | Exactly the channel model (IA-14); the designer's touchstone |
81	| Project Zomboid | Skill levels that shorten action time or cut failure chance | **Reject** | Progression from repair (the Graph writes none, LS-23); would break bar-length identity between a real and a hallucinated job |
82	| Pandorum | Chest-mounted, hands-free lamp: both hands work while lit | **Adopt** | User decision; the beam stays on the job and while carrying |
83	| Barotrauma | Stationary hold-to-repair where interruption is the player's choice, under pressure | **Adopt (the stationary hold)** | The breach-rhythm pressure of Pillar 2 |
84	| Barotrauma | Repair minigame (sliders, wiring) | **Reject** | A minigame is a QTE in disguise (no QTE anywhere) and a UI surface that could leak module-body truth |
85	| Generic action games | Round or dial-shaped progress and confirm indicators; verb menus | **Reject** | Art bible 3.4 / 7.3 and HR-14: the bar is linear with a needle-mark; one contextual action |
86	| Dead Space | Diegetic UI on the character and in the world | **Reject for prompts; adopt the spirit for results** | The prompt is explicitly meta (art bible 7.0) so it can never be corrupted into a lie; results are diegetic (hiss, cold) |
87	| Prompts that name the outcome ("Repair broken pipe") | Verb plus object state | **Reject** | A free oracle under Pillar 4(b); the prompt never names condition |
88	
89	**Tone and language.** Use: reach, hands, hold, the bar, step away, let go, patch, cut, cap, crank, close the breaker, open the valve, throw a glowstick, check, in the light, the edge, chest lamp, beam, go dark, the hiss thins, the room warms, nothing happened. Avoid in player-facing text and in fantasy prose: attack, strike, hit, damage, kill, "target" as an on-screen noun, "failed" or "can't" as a rejection string (the kernel never displays strings), "success!", "repaired!", minigame, QTE, combo, skill, level up, XP, "health" for modules (say the pipe holds or leaks), flashlight or torch for the beam, visibility, stealth, detection, hidden. Prompt grammar is locked by the art bible: keybind plus verb, `E · Patch`, never condition, never target.
90	
91	**Anti-pillar guard rails (stated as fiction as well as rule).**
92	1. *Not a combat game.* There is no attack input. The friendly-harm act is an ordinary tool verb on a crewmate, gated on the *actor's* authoritative Sanity level, lethal against a victim who cannot or does not respond, with the moment of death being Suit's rule (IA-31; "death is a bitch. It happens." — user), with no reward, no counter, no XP and no attribution inside Interaction: one `record_harm_event` call is made to Sanity (registry: `record_harm_event`), which attributes it to the web. Horrors take no verb at MVP; tools repel through Horror and Attention, and nothing is attacked.
93	2. *No intentional PvP.* A sane actor sees no prompt on a crewmate and is rejected `NOT_ELIGIBLE` if they force the attempt.
94	3. *Not a freeform builder.* Weld, section cut and install are pre-shaped and Assembly's; Interaction only declares which button starts them.
95	4. *No meter, no readout, no tooltip.* No interaction stat, no weight readout, no numeric or bar sanity readout, no "you can't do that because…" string; a rejection is a cue, never a shake. **One ruled exception (CD-GDD-ALIGN, recorded):** the actor's *own* sanity level is honest self-knowledge, which Pillar 4 allows. The concept makes the harm gate "verifiably below threshold" and gives the attacker "a visible sanity sign" (CON:252), so the presence of the friendly-harm prompt, and the immediate `NOT_ELIGIBLE` on a forced attempt, are a permitted one-bit statement about the actor's own state and about nothing in the world: no module, no figure, no hallucination class. The prompt is not a gauge of anything else (IA-31).
96	5. *No reward path for work.* No repair score, salvage bonus or faster hands; the reward of a patch is a warm room.
97	
98	**Trade-off accepted.** Some jobs will be three seconds of noise for nothing: the deferred outcome is the price of a sanity system that is not a free lie-detector. We accept that a minority of players will call it "the game wasted my time" in exchange for the majority learning "my eyes are lying." The mitigation is diegetic — the consequence channel (cold, hiss, draught, heat shimmer) lets a careful player decide *before* reaching; reading the world is always cheaper than reaching for it. **We will know this was right if** playtesters describe a failed job as "it wasn't really broken" or "it was still too hot" rather than "the game wouldn't let me" or "bug"; no playtester asks for a "why can't I" message and, asked how they knew a pipe was really fixed, they answer with a physical sign (the cold stopped, the hiss stopped) rather than a UI element; players step away mid-channel when they hear something and do not report feeling punished; and a review finds no channel duration, reason class or prompt rule whose inputs include sanity, Attention, rhythm or device. **Pass/fail threshold:** the attribution half of these criteria is a playtest row, AC-IA-73b (at least 7 of 8 testers who receive a deferred outcome explain it with a physical cause rather than "bug" or "the game wouldn't let me"); a miss re-opens this trade-off, first by strengthening the consequence channel's legibility and never by adding a reason string. The cost to Challenge is therefore measured, not assumed. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review, two additions. (1) The hands answer the world; the scanner answers Sanity. A `field_check` is the cheap way to debunk a lie about an object and is deliberately priced (a tool in hand, `FIELD_CHECK_TICKS`, TOOL noise); a hand job answers what is true of the pipe, at the price of its whole bar. The scanner therefore dominates hand-checking as a way to resolve a hallucination, and that is accepted: it resolves the lie, not the leak (Open Question 32 keeps the repair completion from debunking). (2) The Pillar 3 price of working has to be perceivable: a TOOL push with no tell is a hidden stat. The tell is Attention's (its noise-driven tell and consequence, the owner named in IA-33) voiced by Adaptive Audio; Interaction supplies only the class. AC-IA-136 is the playtest row: a consequence within about 10 s of a TOOL push, named by most testers.)*
99	
100	**What this section does not claim.** The cost of light (Emitter State) and of noise (Attention); the body's honesty and the focus model (Controller); the physics of the hiss, the cold and `BLOCKED` reasons (Graph); trails (Failure & Trail); vitals, charges, the weight cue and death (Suit); what a scanner reveals, the harm threshold, scars and the victim's tell (Sanity, Perception Filter); prompt and bar pixels (HUD); cue sound design (Adaptive Audio). Interaction owns which verb a press means, when it is accepted, how long it takes, and when the answer arrives.

102	## Detailed Design
103	
104	### Core Rules
105	
106	*Conventions.* Rules are numbered `IA-n` (Interaction Act); formulas `D.n` (Formulas section); invariants `I-n`; acceptance criteria `AC-IA-n`; diagnostics `IA_*`. Durations are in ticks (`TICK_RATE` 60); the one seconds-denominated knob, `FULL_JOB_GRACE_S`, converts with the kernel's `ticks_for_seconds`. "Class A" and "Class B" are the Graph's mutator classes (LS-18: Class A is command-backed and paired with a pure `check_*`; Class B is unconditional, clamps and never rejects). Every contract with a system that has no GDD on disk is tagged `(provisional — X undesigned)`; the names given for those contracts are proposals the neighbour must adopt or replace. A contract with a designed sibling is tagged `(Suit & Equipment, Designed — SE-n)` or `(Layout, Designed — LY-n)` and uses the names that GDD publishes (the owner of an interface is the system that publishes it). Where an owner GDD spells only some names of a pattern, an inferred name is tagged as inferred at its first use. Upstream constants and formulas (`in_reach`, `lit(ref)` hysteresis, `fairness_gate`, `repair_part_for`, `salvage_yield`, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` and the rest of the cited list under Tuning Knobs) are used by registry name where registered, else by the owner GDD's own identifier (Cross-References section 5 lists the 12 names not yet registered), and never restated; where this GDD needs a different value that is a CONFLICT, surfaced in Open Questions, never a silent change. Each rule names what decides it ("*Decides:*") and, where one existed, the alternative considered. Where the four specialist proposals disagreed and the advisor rulings were silent, the choice is marked "(orchestrator ruling: …)". Where a specialist proposed a departure from an advisor ruling and the checkpoint rejected it (DEP-1, DEP-3), the ruling stays in the text and the departure is recorded in Open Questions as a closed alternative with the checkpoint reason.

108	**Group A — Ownership, declaration, focus and the lit-only rule**
109	
110	**IA-1 Interaction is the verb layer, not a doer of everything.** Interaction (a) declares, per focused object and equipped tool, which command type and mode a press of `interact` means; (b) registers the command types whose effect is its own (IA-3); (c) owns channel progress, partial-progress persistence, pickup, drop, throw, the field check, the friendly-harm act and revive; (d) is the caller of the Graph's Class A mutators M6 to M9 and M11 to M13 (M10 has no MVP verb) for the player verbs, of the Class B M16 for V7 top-up, and of Emitter State's subject registration (E6, E7, E8) and `spawn_deployable` (E3); (e) publishes exactly three Class B mutators (`sync_section`, `place_loose`, and `open_channel` for owner-registered channels, IA-35), two read views (`focus_view`, `channel_view`) and one pure derived read (`last_salvage_T()`, IA-25), and nothing else. It never draws, never subscribes to results and never calls presentation (kernel CR-10); it uses no RNG and no wall-clock (every outcome is a deterministic function of block state, true Graph state and the tick); it holds no scene-tree reference (H10). *Decides:* advisor R1, guard G1, kernel CR-10.
111	
112	**IA-2 The declaration table is data.** One row per (object class, tool requirement) under `assets/data/interaction/verbs/` — the folder the Controller's lint already scans. Fields: `verb_id` (a V-id or an Interaction id); `object_class` (BREAKER_PANEL, VALVE, DOOR_FACE, VENT_HATCH, REPAIRABLE, SALVAGE_MODULE, CRANK_MACHINE, WELD_SOCKET, STUB, LOOSE_ITEM, SWITCH_FIXTURE, ACTOR, ACTOR_SELF, TOPUP_PORT, INSTRUMENT, HARDPOINT, CONSOLE (two classes, POD_CONSOLE and DOCK_CONSOLE, told apart by Layout's `console_role`, IA-40 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ASK-CT-13 / ASK-CT-14 accepted, delegated G6, GAP)*); one interactable may carry several classes — a scrubber is both REPAIRABLE and SALVAGE_MODULE); `command_type`; `owner_system`; `mode` in {TAP, HOLD_CONFIRM, CHANNEL}; `tool_required` (a def id or NONE); `noise_class` in {QUIET, TOOL, LOUD}; `duration_key` (names a registered constant, never a literal); `reason_classes` (per reason, IMMEDIATE or DEFERRED); `verb_name_key` (a localisation key; always state-neutral, IA-11); `eligible` (an optional predicate name; at MVP: Sanity's `actor_sanity_below_harm_threshold` (registry; IA-31), Assembly's `weld_offer` and `seam_cut_offer` (registry; IA-23) and Web Map's `console_ready(role)`, with `berthed_present()` for the two DOCK_CONSOLE rows (WM-8; IA-40); an owner-supplied predicate is evaluated exactly as Interaction's own and reads no module-body field, IA-11b); `admitted_while_carrying` (bool, default false; true only on the HARDPOINT `install_module` row, the POD_CONSOLE `pod_hop` row and the door `set_opening` row, IA-28; *Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the door row added*) (registry: `admitted_while_carrying`); `destructive` (bool); `priority` (int, for IA-5); `subject_allowed` (bool, so that in-wall cable and duct edges are repaired at their visible junction, not along their length). The table takes **no** sanity, Attention, rhythm, breach, device or hold-versus-toggle input (lint, IA-4). A pull request that adds a verb is one data row, one handler and one registration line, with an empty Adapter diff (Controller acceptance stub at PCI:969; kernel velocity rule, KRN:135). *Decides:* R1, R26, PC-6.

114	**IA-3 One command type per verb; `interact` is an input action.** Each verb is its own command type with its own `validate`, reason subset, `max_age_ticks` 120 (`MAX_AGE_TICKS_ACTION`; `STALE` is unreachable from local ingress), `coalesce NONE` (edge-triggered), `actor_binding OWNED_BY_ISSUER` with `actor_source body.state` (the acting avatar's Body `actor_id`; kernel CR-7 keys the authority check `(body.state, actor)`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: kernel CR-6 / CR-7 make `actor_source` mandatory on every `OWNED_BY_ISSUER` type, else boot fails `ACTOR_SOURCE_INVALID`; every Interaction type acts as the avatar)*, `allowed_origins {PLAYER}` and not `allowed_when_paused`. Payloads are primitives only (kernel CR-4): a registered subject ref (or a PlayerId for `begin_harm` and `begin_revive`) and, for `throw_glowstick`, `aim_angle` — **never a believed state, a direction, a verb choice or a kind** (LS-22; the one enum, `field_check`'s closed `check_kind` {SCAN}, names the instrument's check, not a subject's kind). 197	**Reason precedence (one global order; orchestrator ruling: qa-lead's order adopted, compatible with the locked CR-7 order of IA-31 and the V7 chain).** When a press fails several conditions at once, `validate` returns the first of: (1) kernel authority and admission reasons (`ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`, `PAUSED`); (2) `NO_TOOL`; (3) `OUT_OF_RANGE` (the geometric conjuncts of `in_reach`); (4) `NOT_LIT`; (5) `BUSY`; (6) `INVALID_TARGET` and the declared kind check; (7) `NOT_ELIGIBLE`; (8) the stock reasons (Suit's `STACK_FULL` and `ALREADY_FULL`, and `OUT_OF_CHARGES`) and `OBSTRUCTED`. A verb that lacks a reason skips its slot (a `drop` has only `INVALID_TARGET` and `OBSTRUCTED`; `begin_crank` has no `NO_TOOL`; `throw_glowstick` has only `BUSY` then `OUT_OF_CHARGES`). Every reason in the order is IMMEDIATE, so the order itself reads no module-body field.

(b) **Prompt existence is a function of (object classes, tool in hand, `lit`, `in_reach`, the `eligible` predicate) only.** A repairable-kind subject prompts regardless of its true hp; a missing prompt on a hallucinated-broken healthy pipe would be a free oracle. (c) **Channel duration and bar length are identical for a hallucinated-broken healthy pipe, a truly broken one and a DESTROYED one** — durations are fixed per verb, and PATCH versus FULL is decided by the actor's own stock (IA-18), never by hp. (d) No payload carries a believed state, a direction or a kind (including PLAYER-origin `set_switch`: `{emitter_id}` only, IA-3). (e) No simulation code (validate, apply, hook) reads a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block (CR-12). (f) The label a prompt shows is state-neutral: V3, V4 and V5 are toggles whose target position is computed from true state at apply, so their `verb_name_key` is `verb_breaker`, `verb_door`, `verb_valve` (or a neutral "use"), and a SWITCH_FIXTURE's is `verb_switch`, and V6's is `verb_vent_hatch`, never "open", "close" or "reset" — a label derived from true state would be a condition readout (art bible 7.0), and one derived from perceived state would be a believed state leaking into the payload. FULL repair and `begin_harm` therefore write `blocks_done` like every other channel; the former wording credited only the non-incremental verbs and left them out. `blocks` in IA-18, D.7 and States and Transitions 5 **is** this `blocks_done` field, and `t_last_block` is persisted in the channel record (States and Transitions 8).)* |

224	Properties (each is an acceptance row): (a) the lit check at `e = 0` re-reads tick T after `validate` read T−1, so a lamp that died in between aborts at progress 0; (b) a lamp that dies at `e = 6j + 1` lets ticks `6j + 1 … 6j + 5` accrue (**five dark ticks at most**, matching Emitter State AC-59b), and the check at `e = 6j + 6` aborts *before* block `j + 1` is credited, so no step and no ledger credit is ever earned on an unlit block end; (c) a lamp that flickers off and on again inside one block costs nothing and the block is credited; (d) a move on `e = D` leaves `blocks_done = n − 1` (PC-7: "one tick short" — the move wins); (e) steps land at `Tb + 6, Tb + 12, …`, never on `Tb`; (f) rows 4 to 6 test `e mod LIT_RECHECK_TICKS == 0`, not `e mod B`, and invariant I-1 (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS mod LIT_RECHECK_TICKS == 0`) makes every block end a check tick, so no step is credited on an unlit or out-of-reach block end under any legal retune of `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS`. **The Graph-read lag, stated and not hidden:** the Graph's three hooks run on `T mod 6 == 0` (power), `2` (atmo) and `4` (failure) (Graph LS-8), and each runs *before* `interaction.step` on its tick (through the `emitter.place` chain). A step applied at tick `Tb + 6j` is read by the hook that consumes that mutator's effect on the first of its ticks strictly after the apply: hp changes (M7/M8/M10-class) by the failure hook (phases 8-9, `T mod 6 == 4`), requests and loads (M14, M13 valve/breaker) by the power hook (phases 0-2, `T mod 6 == 0`). The lag is the distance to the next such tick, 1 to 6 ticks in every case (≤ 100 ms); the range is unchanged. "The hiss stops when hp crosses `LEAK_HP`" therefore trails the step by up to one Graph step; this is the honest timing. *Alternative considered:* steps only on the failure-hook tick (`T mod 6 == 4`) — removes the lag variance but makes the effective duration 180 to 185 ticks and the bar length depend on the begin offset (rejected). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: the former derivation assumed the three Graph hooks share `T mod 6 == 0`; under the Graph's baseline stagger, offsets 0/2/4, they do not. Recomputed: the [1, 6] tick range is unchanged.)* A channel never locks movement; the facing locks during a channel (Controller behaviour, `FACING_HYSTERESIS`). A pause does not interrupt a channel — the tick simply does not advance (CR-16). *Decides:* R9, R10, L46 (PC-7), EM-25, R4.
225	
226	**IA-15 Abort causes, cues, no buffering.** The closed set of abort causes: `MOVED`, `CANCELLED`, `UNLIT`, `OUT_OF_REACH`, `TARGET_GONE`, `BODY` (stagger, downed, body transfer, seat rebind — the sub-cause is diagnostic), `NOT_ELIGIBLE`, `RESTORE`. A channel record ends in exactly one terminal state: `DONE`, `ABORT(cause)` or `OUTCOME(sub)` (IA-12); when `cancel_channel` and an abort cause fall on the same tick, `cancel_channel` (P2) wins and the hook finds no record. A `cancel_channel` with no channel is **Applied as a no-op** (counted `IA_CANCEL_NOOP`), not rejected: the Adapter sends `cancel` on every hold release, and a reject there would play the dull "no" cue after every completed channel. Cues are specified in Visual/Audio Requirements and Game Feel; their *meaning* is fixed here: cancel (the player let go) drains the bar; abort (the world or the body ended it) snaps the bar empty with a distinct "interrupted" cue; completion fills it; a deferred outcome fills it and then plays "nothing happened"; an immediate rejection withdraws the acknowledgement within one frame with a dull cue and no shake *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the withdrawal alone is sub-perceptible, and a mashed press could flicker it faster than the 3 Hz ceiling. The HUD therefore holds the restored keycap in a one-step Graphite-lit state for `BAR_REJECT_HOLD_TICKS` (HUD-owned, proposed 9, safe range 6 to 18) and admits at most one reject presentation per seat per `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS`; the rejection stays a cut and a cue, never a shake)*. "Stopped", "interrupted" and "nothing happened" are three different sounds and three different shapes. `ACTION_BUFFER_TICKS` is 0: a press during a channel is submitted and answered `BUSY`; nothing queues for "after" (PCI:84). The abort cause is delivered to presentation as diagnostic data only and the HUD never reads it; the one bit the HUD needs, the player's own cancel versus every world cause, is the non-diagnostic `channel_view.ended_by` (IA-41): one drain for `PLAYER_CANCEL`, one abort frame set and one abort cue for every `WORLD` cause (HUD & Suit Layer OQ-HS-19). *Decides:* L47, L49, R10.
227	
228	**IA-16 Partial progress.** *Incremental repair needs no ledger* (advisor R9): an abort leaves hp physically raised by the steps already applied, which is honest. **Non-incremental channels** (`begin_cut`, `begin_cap`, `begin_crank`, `field_check`, `begin_revive`, and Assembly's `begin_weld` and `begin_seam_cut`, whose records are Interaction's, IA-35) write a ledger entry on abort keyed `(seat, subject_ref, verb_id)` = `{blocks_done, abort_tick, n}` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: `n` added so a retuned duration discards the entry, D.6; **`begin_harm` is removed from this list, delegated G2 following the creative-director's BLOCKING reading of the D36 ruling**: a harm re-begin always restarts at `e = 0` with its own full escape window, because the cumulative damage already persists in the victim's Suit integrity and a resumed bar would put the next damage 6 ticks after the re-begin, defeating the 65-tick walking window that D36 guarantees)*. A re-begin by the same seat on the same subject and verb with `T − abort_tick ≤ PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` (inclusive) resumes: `resume_offset = blocks_done × B`, the remaining time is `(n − blocks_done) × B` ticks, and the bar continues from `blocks_done / n` (the bar is a function of declared duration and the player's own history, never of any module-body field, IA-11c). After `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` the entry is gone; it is also deleted on `DONE` or an outcome. The ledger is bounded by `MAX_PARTIAL_ENTRIES` per seat; when full, the entry with the smallest `abort_tick` is evicted (ties: the smallest `subject_ref`); expiry is evaluated every tick in the hook so snapshot contents are replay-stable. The ledger ages on global ticks whatever the subject's section is doing: an entry on a dormant derelict's subject expires `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` after its abort like any other, so a partial cut never survives a hop leg (600 ticks against a 945-tick leg; Boarding ASK-BS-I5). A `BODY` abort still credits finished blocks. Noise is pushed only for newly accrued ticks, so splitting a job does not reduce its total noise, only spreads it. *Why a short TTL:* no persistence punishes a cancel-to-peek, which is the Pillar 2 behaviour "I can leave now"; permanent persistence is a free ratchet for splitting a noise burst; proportional decay is more state for no gain. *Constraint on a neighbour:* splitting a job reduces peak Attention only if the gap is comparable to Attention's noise memory `TAU_ATT_TICKS` (1800, registry); `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS ≤ 2 × TAU_ATT_TICKS` is accepted by Attention (registry `noise_unit_relations` IR-3; Attention System, Designed — AT-3). *For incremental repair hp is the ledger:* a re-begin recomputes D.1 from the then-current hp over the full block count, so the work already applied is kept and the only loss on a one-tick-short abort is a fresh bar for the last block's basis points (a block-granular ledger for repair was proposed and rejected at the checkpoint: a second record of the same quantity could disagree with hp after M7 clamps, decay, `apply_damage` or another seat's repair). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **a restore writes no ledger entry.** `post_restore` drops the in-progress channel as `ABORT(RESTORE)` for presentation purposes only; it neither creates a partial-progress entry from the dropped record nor refreshes `abort_tick` of an existing one, so a save-restore cycle can neither start nor extend a resume window; entries that survived the snapshot keep their absolute `abort_tick` and age on global ticks as before. The one persisted record a restore does touch is the FULL-job part record, which commits or releases by the blocks-credited rule (IA-18); that is a part-stock transition, not a ledger entry. The honest cost of leaving, restated for the Player Fantasy: hp already raised stays; a cut, cap, crank or field check resumes only within `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`; a resumed PATCH recomputes over the full bar.)* *Decides:* R9, PCI Open Question 7.
229	
230	**Group D — Repair, the part, and the patch**
231	
232	**IA-17 Repair is real, incremental `repair_step`.** For `begin_patch` the hook, at every credited block (IA-14 row 8), calls `check_repair_step` and then M7 `repair_step(subject_kind, id, delta_bp, kind)` with `delta_bp` = `repair_step_delta` (D.1). `hp_at_begin` is read in the hook at the first step, never in `validate` (IA-11a). **Healthy-subject guard (Interaction's own, independent of the Graph's answer to the hp-clamp question):** the hook never calls M7 PATCH when `hp_at_begin ≥ LEAK_HP` **and** `cap_at_begin > PATCH_CAP_BP` (the subject has never been patched and nothing is leaking), and never calls M7 at all when `repair_step_delta ≤ 0`; such a job runs its full duration with zero mutator calls and resolves `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING, delegated G2 (the creative-director's Option B): the former threshold, `hp_at_begin` at or above the patch cap itself, left the silent band open: at true hp 4000 to 5999 a PATCH gained at most 1999 bp, permanently lowered `hp_cap` by 4000 bp and emitted the Graph's patch weep, which a healthy pipe does not, so a one-block tap-and-cancel probed a pipe's true state at the price of a block, the P4 failure Design Test 2 names. The guard is now keyed on the real harm: **both** `hp_at_begin` and `cap_at_begin` are read in the hook at the first step (the Graph's `node()` / `edge()` carry `hp_cap`, as M6's `SalvageRecord` does). A PATCH on a subject that is not leaking and has never been patched is "not a job a patch can do": silent damage is FULL work (Pillar 5), and the job runs the full bar and resolves `NOTHING_TO_REPAIR` identically at hp 10000, 5999, 5000 and 4000 with `hp_cap` 10000, with identical Graph state, descriptors and noise. Resume and top-up are kept: a half-patched subject has `hp_cap` = `PATCH_CAP_BP`, so the guard does not fire and the job continues (AC-IA-15, AC-IA-27, AC-IA-143, D.1 example 5). Leaking subjects (hp below `LEAK_HP`) are patched as before: their cold and hiss already tell the player. The Graph-side cure (M7 PATCH never lowers `hp_cap`, no weep before completion) stays open for the Graph owner (Open Question 10) and would make the guard a pure optimisation.)* A Graph answer `ABOVE_PATCH_CAP`, if M7 ever returns one, maps at the end of the bar to `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)` as well (D.3), never to a distinct token. *Why:* otherwise a hallucinated-broken healthy pipe (hp `HP_FULL`) would have its `hp_cap` written down to `PATCH_CAP_BP` by LS-23 and go permanently DEGRADED — a hallucination physically damaging a module, breaking Pillars 1 and 4 together. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; **superseded by the re-review amendment above, which moves the guard to `LEAK_HP` and `cap_at_begin`**: the `PATCH_CAP_BP` threshold of the guard is arbitrary, and its residual is wider than "1 bp for a cap write". A hallucinated-broken pipe whose true hp lies in 4000 to 5999 is silent (no leak, because `hp ≥ LEAK_HP`), so no consequence channel warns the player, and a PATCH on it raises hp by at most 1999 bp while permanently writing `hp_cap` from 10000 down to 6000, a loss of 4000 bp of ceiling. The preferred cure is the Graph's: **M7 PATCH never lowers `hp_cap`** (it only ever raises `hp`, up to `min(hp_cap, PATCH_CAP_BP)`), which makes the guard a pure optimisation; this is routed to the Graph owner and must be answered before the repair story (Open Question 10). The interim recording of the damage range in Edge Cases B and AC-IA-90 is replaced by the guard.)* A hallucinated-fixed pipe at true hp 2000 receives real increments against 2000; its cold and its hiss persist until true hp crosses `LEAK_HP` (LS-22). A DESTROYED subject is never repairable (LS-23): the first `check_repair_step` fails, zero mutator calls, the job runs its full duration and resolves `PRECONDITION(NOT_REPAIRABLE)`. **Class A calls from a P3 hook are legal:** LSG:176 ("callable only inside a kernel-issued `WriteScope` in P2/P3") and LSG:186 (M7's caller is "Interaction (`begin_patch` channel steps)") both say so, and kernel CR-9 (KRN:104: a hook uses a published unconditional mutator or a SYSTEM-origin command) is satisfied because every step is check-then-apply: the check precedes the apply, a failing check skips the apply, and `apply` therefore stays infallible and is never FAULTED. A reader of CR-9 alone may object; both citations are given here for that reason. **The self-patch (object class ACTOR_SELF; Suit & Equipment, Designed — SE-22 / SE-40).** A declaration row of object class ACTOR_SELF (welder in hand, CHANNEL, `PATCH_CHANNEL_TICKS`, noise TOOL, payload `{target_ref}` = the actor's own PlayerId) lets the actor patch their own suit; its apply calls `set_channel_ref(actor, INTERACTION, channel_id, NONE)`: ACTOR_SELF has no target anchor, so `face_octant = NONE` and the Controller holds `facing_prev` for the channel (PCI D.8 rule 2) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6/G1, CONFLICT)*. Its incremental steps run at the IA-14 cadence and call Suit's `patch_integrity(actor, delta)` with `delta` from D.1 evaluated against `SUIT_PATCH_CAP_BP` (Suit's symbol, cited, never restated) and `integrity_bp` read **in the hook**, never in `validate`; the same healthy-subject guard applies (no call when `integrity_bp` already meets the cap; the job resolves `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)`). There is no part and no FULL variant at MVP. The actor's own body is the honest actor channel, so reading `integrity_bp` is not an oracle question. The self-patch is an `act_gate`-exempt actor verb (IA-6) and, with the welder in hand, the Controller's focus (PC-6 self-target rule, fallback when no lit candidate is in reach and arc) makes it startable from the `interact` button with the lamp on or off; the focus never depends on `integrity_bp` (the guard above handles a healthy suit) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP: the owner adds the surface the Controller's ruled behaviour needs; IA-4, IA-5, IA-41 `self_target`)*: lamp on or off, with no other light, the press is accepted and the channel is not aborted `UNLIT`. *Resolved 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6 (GAP; the Controller's PC-6 option (a) is the spec; Emitter State's EM-21 rule that the owner's beam adds nothing to the owner's `act_lux_pm` stays intact, option (b) is not taken).* The self-patch story is no longer blocked. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated G6, GAP: the owner adds the surface the Controller's ruled behaviour needs. Replaces the 2026-10-27 routed acceptance condition and the design-review note that blocked the story.)* MVP if and only if Suit's integrity axis is MVP (SE-22 lists MVP damage sources, so it is). *Decides:* R4, R9, LS-18, LS-22, LS-23, Suit SE-22.
233	
234	**IA-18 PATCH versus FULL, the part reservation, and the Item DB's AC-40 statements.** FULL if and only if the actor holds `parts_per_full` of `repair_part_for(subject_kind, kind_id, loop)` (`repair_part_for` cited by registry name, `parts_per_full` by the Item DB's own name; neither restated), or already holds a PAID record for the subject (a RESERVED record exists only while that seat's channel runs); otherwise PATCH. The choice is made in `validate` from the actor's own stock (the honest actor channel), so the channel's duration never depends on hp. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the stock rule above removes a decision. Whenever a part is stowed FULL is selected automatically, so a player cannot spend a cheap patch on a minor leak and keep the deep-derelict part for a real repair; that removes the Pillar 5 resource choice and fails Autonomy (SDT). **The selector is the actor's declaration, not their stock:** FULL if and only if the actor holds `parts_per_full` of the part **and has it readied** in Suit's hand rail (`part_ready(player_id, def_id)`, the actor's own selection, read in `validate`; reuses the IA-5 idea of "what is in hand"; a read of the actor's own state, never of hp, so it is no oracle), or already holds a PAID record for the subject; otherwise PATCH. A player holding the part who has not readied it completes a PATCH with the part untouched (AC-IA-135). The false claim that the bar class is "visible before the press" is withdrawn from Game Feel: `focus_view.duration_class` shows LONG pre-press only to a player who readied the part, which is their own choice told back to them, and nothing else on the plate shows the length class before the press. **Provisional on Suit:** `part_ready` and the hand-rail readying are a Suit ask (Open Question 42, cross-GDD note). Until Suit answers, the stock rule above stays in force as an interim and the autonomy defect stays open, labelled.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated G2 (creative-director: this undermines Pillar 5 more than any number): **the MVP selector is chosen, and there is one: the stock rule, with a mandatory pre-press tell.** The `part_ready` selector above is **not** an MVP rule: it rests on a Suit API that does not exist (the selector was "provisional on Suit" while IA-41, D.13 and AC-IA-91 already read it as fact), so two selectors lived in the same document. At MVP: FULL iff the actor's own stock holds `parts_per_full` of `repair_part_for(subject_kind, kind_id, loop)` or a PAID record exists, else PATCH; the commit at 100 ms is no longer an ambush because `focus_view` carries `part_tell` (IA-41), a bool true iff the focused V1 subject's declared kind has a repair part (`repair_part_for` not NONE) and the actor's own stowed count meets `parts_per_full`, drawn as a second notch on the keycap with no colour, numeral or pip (form proposed, HUD & Suit Layer owns the asset). It is a function of the declared kind and the actor's own stock only, never of hp or module-body state, so it is no oracle. A player who does not want to spend the part on this subject has the whole pre-press window to look elsewhere; a press that commits inside the first `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` costs nothing, and the Game Feel text now says exactly that. The `part_ready` / hand-rail selector stays the Suit ask of Open Question 42 as a **post-MVP upgrade** that would give the player an explicit choice; where it lands it replaces the stock rule and the tell changes meaning to "readied". Every "readied" in IA-41, D.13, AC-IA-91 and AC-IA-135 is therefore the post-MVP form, marked as such.)* The following statements discharge Item DB AC-40 and are normative:
235	1. `repair_part_for` returning `NONE` means **no FULL job is ever offered** on that subject (PATCH only); there is no `BLOCKED` for a missing part — FULL is simply not offered without it. (A SEAM subject returns `NONE`; a seam is restored by V9 re-weld.)
236	2. **A PATCH consumes no item.**
237	3. A FULL job issues only `kind = FULL` steps (IDB AC-38); a job never mixes kinds.
238	4. **A seat's part is spent when that seat's first productive step is applied** — a step that raises `hp` or raises `hp_cap` — through Suit's `consume_reserved` (Suit & Equipment, Designed — SE-41). A whole subject costs time and no part if no step is ever productive. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: restated by the commit rule below. A part is spent at the first productive step, or, if no step was productive, when the channel ends by cancel, abort or restore after at least one block was credited; it comes back only when the bar runs to its end with no productive step. "Costs time and no part" therefore holds only for a bar that runs to the end.)*
239	5. A FULL job interrupted after its first productive step keeps the part spent and the hp; there is no refund (IDB AC-38). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the same holds for a job interrupted after its first credited block, productive or not, so that the two truth branches cannot be told apart by what the interruption returns.)*

content.content:
240	6. A FULL job re-issued by **the same seat on the same subject** within `FULL_JOB_GRACE_S` (Interaction's own constant, 60 s [PLACEHOLDER], carrying the Item DB's resume-allowance recommendation) is not charged again; other seats are charged. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the grace is measured from the last credited block of the interrupted job, not from the last productive step, so its length does not depend on module-body state.)*
241	7. A FULL job on a subject already at `hp_cap = HP_FULL` with `hp = hp_cap` consumes nothing and resolves `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)` as an Applied-and-did-nothing outcome *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: only if the bar runs to its end; cancelled after a credited block it consumes the part exactly as it would on a damaged subject)*.
242	8. PATCH on a subject that is not leaking (`hp ≥ LEAK_HP`) and has never been patched (`hp_cap > PATCH_CAP_BP`): the prompt still appears (IA-11b); the job resolves `NOTHING_TO_REPAIR` unless the actor holds the part, in which case it is a FULL job — the Item DB's "offer only FULL there" reading is adopted as behaviour, and the hp-clamp question stays routed to the Graph owner. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING: was "a subject whose `hp` already exceeds `PATCH_CAP_BP`"; the guard of IA-17 is keyed on the real harm.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: "holds the part" reads "has the part readied" under the declaration selector above.)*
243	9. DESTROYED is never repairable (IA-17): the path is salvage (scrap) then install.
244	
245	**Part reservation and the commit rule (closes an oracle; orchestrator ruling, rewritten by the design review).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review, BLOCKING: the former reservation released the part at `until = Tb + FULL_CHANNEL_TICKS` whatever the player did, so a player could press a FULL job, cancel at e = 7 to 10, walk away and read the pack at `until`: the part returned only if the module was truly healthy (a hallucination). That is a lie detector priced at "time and a held resource" the player pays while standing nowhere near the pipe, not lit, not loud, so its Pillar 3 and Pillar 4 price (exposure plus TOOL noise) was about 2 to 3 % of the channel's, and the former Edge Case and AC-IA-30 pinned the leak as correct. The creative-director ruling, game-designer's form, replaces it: the reservation outcome is **branch-independent** from the first moment the two truth branches could differ.)*
246	
247	*Reservation.* When a FULL job is Applied, the part enters the state `RESERVED`. Suit treats a RESERVED or PAID part as having left the pack, in the stock count, in the carried mass that drives the weight cue and in its `reserved` bucket, **from the begin tick, in both truth branches** (SE-41). The record carries no timer: `until` is retired, and there is no expiry sweep.
248	
249	*The commit rule.* Let `blocks` be the number of blocks the channel has credited (IA-14 row 8). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: `blocks` **is** the channel record's `blocks_done`, written by row 8 for FULL repair like every other verb, and `t_last_block` is the record's persisted field of the same name; a FULL job is never resumed through the ledger, so `blocks_done` is the run's own count.)* A block is credited in both truth branches whether or not its step was productive, so `blocks` is a branch-independent counter. The channel ends in exactly one terminal state, and the part record resolves with it:
250	1. **`DONE`.** The part was consumed at the first productive step (statement 4, `consume_reserved`); the record is `PAID(grace_until)` until the same hook run's completion closes it (NONE; the job is finished, so there is nothing left to resume) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: PAID is closed by the `DONE` event itself, never by a test of hp, see Re-begin below)*.
251	2. **`OUTCOME`** (the bar ran to its end and no step was productive: `NOTHING_TO_REPAIR`, `NOT_REPAIRABLE`). **This is the only path that returns a part:** `release_stowed`, the record becomes NONE. The `NOTHING_TO_REPAIR` outcome is the deferred reveal, paid for with the full bar.
252	3. **`cancel_channel`, any `ABORT(cause)` (`MOVED`, `UNLIT`, `OUT_OF_REACH`, `TARGET_GONE`, `BODY`, `NOT_ELIGIBLE`) or a restore** (a restore drops the channel as `ABORT(RESTORE)`, IA-36):
253	   - **`blocks = 0`** (the channel ended before its first block was credited): no step has been applied in either branch, the two branches are identical, and the part is released at once in both (`release_stowed`, record NONE).
254	   - **`blocks ≥ 1`**: the part is consumed **in both truth branches** (`consume_reserved` if it is still RESERVED; already consumed if a productive step made it PAID) and the record is `PAID(grace_until)` with `grace_until = t_last_block + ticks_for_seconds(FULL_JOB_GRACE_S)`, `t_last_block` the tick of the last credited block. A truly healthy module and a truly damaged one therefore leave the stock, the weight cue and the reserved bucket identical at every tick after any cancel, abort or restore. 286	**IA-28 Pickup, drop, loose items.** Interaction owns `loose[]` in `interaction.state` — `{item_id, section_id, pos_px, inst}` with the position **section-local** (`section_id`, `pos_px`; Layout LY-22: "a weld or a detach moves nothing") — and registers an ITEM subject for each (EM-24: "Interaction owns the dropped-item registrations"). `inst` is the Item DB ItemInstance in its only persisted and hashed form, the six-element array from `to_array()` = `[def_id, count, condition_bp, cap_bp, patched_at_step, charge]` (IDB-15/16, registry `item_instance_to_array`); there is no separate `def_id` and no separate condition field — the def is `inst[0]`, one copy, so the two cannot diverge. `item_id` stays outside the instance (IDB-15: an instance id is not schema) and is minted from `next_item_id`, or reused from the `(instance_id, instance)` pair that `release_carried` returns. A STOWED-class def validates with Suit's `can_stow(player_id, inst[0], inst[1])` and is rejected with Suit's own immediate reason **`STACK_FULL`** (actor stock; Suit-namespaced) when the stack cannot take it; otherwise it moves LOOSE_WORLD → STOWED through Suit's `add_stowed(player_id, inst)` with the entry's `inst` unchanged, merging per IDB-15. A thrower who dies while a stick is in flight still sees it land (a world object). `THROW_RANGE_TILES` 3 (1 to 5) and `THROW_ARC_TICKS` 30 (15 to 60) are registered as Interaction's [PLACEHOLDER] at exactly the values the Controller (D.16), the Item DB (IDB:259) and Emitter State (EM:198) already cite (F1: a placeholder in a table of record becomes a fact). 290	**IA-30 Field check.** `field_check {subject_ref, check_kind}`; the MVP `check_kind` is SCAN only (scanner in hand; Vertical Slice A adds HEFT, the lift-and-weigh, and PALETTE). A lit-only CHANNEL of `FIELD_CHECK_TICKS`, ledger-resumable. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review, BLOCKING: **the call site is the hook on the completion tick, never `apply`.** In this GDD `apply` runs at the begin tick, so a call from `apply` would have Sanity DEBUNK an active lie at e = 0, a free oracle at the press (the lie ends, or visibly does not, before any time, light or noise is spent); the `outcome` argument also exists only at completion. The hook calls `record_falsification` exactly once, **on the terminal tick of the channel, whether it ends `DONE` or `OUTCOME`** (IA-14 row 9; the SCAN check has no body-state outcome at MVP, so `DONE` is the live case), and **never** at begin, at a resume-begin from the ledger, on `cancel_channel`, on any `ABORT(cause)` or on a restore.)* The hook then calls the Sanity-owned Class B mutator `record_falsification(player_id, check_kind, subject_ref, outcome)` (registry: `record_falsification`; Sanity & Hallucination Rules, Designed), which writes a **Sanity SIM block**; `outcome` is the channel result only, and Sanity derives whether a lie existed from its own ledger (Sanity C5); what the scanner reveals and whether it can itself lie is Sanity's. **No check result is ever stored in `interaction.state` as truth about a lie** (CR-12). The second-instrument check is a different gauge elsewhere on the ship, reached by walking there and `inspect` (art bible 7.0), never the inspect card of the suspect gauge; the scanner reading, and `suit.o2` / `suit.warmth` for the seat's current compartment (`suit.warmth` for the COOLANT loop's thermal quantity only), also count as rung-2 instruments (Sanity L-2I, C21); any simulation-visible falsification result is a `field_check`. The cost is time, light, a tool in hand and noise: the declared noise class is TOOL (the scanner loop, pushed per accrued tick, IA-33), so a stationary scan is never free of Attention (Sanity OQ-SN-13). Calling `record_falsification` from REPAIR or INSPECT completions is not adopted (Open Question 32). *Decides:* R14, KRN:202, IDX:25.

292	**IA-31 The friendly-harm act.** `begin_harm {target_player}` is a CHANNEL declared for object class ACTOR with the **cutter or welder** in hand, `HARM_CHANNEL_TICKS`. The gate order in `validate` is locked (kernel CR-7): (1) kernel authority (the issuer owns the actor); (2) the immediate checks — tool (`NO_TOOL`), `act_gate` (`OUT_OF_RANGE`, `NOT_LIT`), `BUSY`; (3) the target is an ACTOR subject whose PlayerId differs from the actor's (`INVALID_TARGET`); (4) Sanity's `actor_sanity_below_harm_threshold(player_id)` (registry: `actor_sanity_below_harm_threshold`; false for an unknown PlayerId) over the SIM sanity-level block, **never `PERCEPTION_OUT`** (`NOT_ELIGIBLE`) *(Sanity & Hallucination Rules, Designed)*; (5) apply. The declaration's `eligible` predicate is the same query, so **no prompt appears for a sane actor** (no accidental harm, no intentional PvP). The prompt's `verb_name_key` is the equipped tool's ordinary verb (`verb_cut` or `verb_weld`) and **never** a target noun — a noun would make the HUD an oracle over a crewmate drawn as a monster (art bible 7.0: keybind and verb, never condition). The effect: every `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` of progress, Suit's Class B `apply_suit_damage(victim, HARM_BP_PER_STEP, source)` *(Suit & Equipment, Designed — SE-40)*, with `HARM_BP_PER_STEP` from D.8, totalling at least `HARM_TOTAL_BP` (10200 at the defaults). **What Interaction guarantees, and what is Suit's.** A completed act delivers `HARM_TOTAL_BP ≥ SUIT_HP_FULL` as EXOGENOUS damage through `apply_suit_damage(victim, HARM_BP_PER_STEP, source_ref)` (`source_ref` classed EXOGENOUS, Suit & Equipment, Designed — SE-23; the build relation `HARM_TOTAL_BP ≥ SUIT_HP_FULL` is registered on this side, Suit's symbol cited). **When death arrives is Suit's rule** (LS-13 "player death is Suit's rule"; SE-23, SE-24): `source_ref` is classed EXOGENOUS, so with `SUIT_EXO_BYPASS_LIMITER` at its default 1 (SE-23; Suit OQ-3 records it as the data form of the user's lethality decision) the integrity rung is set from the new `integrity_bp` on the run after each per-step apply, with no hold — STRAINED below `SUIT_HP_OK`, CRITICAL (the Controller's stagger on the falling edge, then walk-only) below `SUIT_LEAK_HP`, FAILED (cap NONE) below `SUIT_HP_FAIL` (Suit's symbols, cited). The victim's rung therefore tracks the damage inside the channel; a completed act leaves the victim FAILED (cap NONE, DOWNED) on the run after the last step; the victim's Pillar 2 tell is the channel itself (the tool loop and sparks, AD-7) and D.8's escape arithmetic, not the SE-17 hold floor. The first integrity band brings no stagger (the cap is FULL at STRAINED, SE-16; the stagger is CRITICAL's falling edge); the victim may self-patch (IA-17) while above `SUIT_HP_FAIL`; FAILED → `locomotion_cap` `NONE` → DOWNED → DEAD after `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` unless an axis leaves FAILED or a `begin_revive` lands (IA-32) — which is what gives revive an owner. With the knob flipped to 0 (a data flip, reversible by the user only) the uniform limiter applies to every source and FAILED arrives no sooner than the SE-17 floor (AC-SE-24). The user's decision is honoured: the act is lethal and permanent against a victim who cannot or does not respond, and Pillar 2's tell window is honoured for the victim. Completion requires the victim to remain in reach for the whole channel; a conscious victim with room to run takes only part of `HARM_TOTAL_BP` (D.8). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: "room to run" has a cliff that D.8 now states. The step that drops integrity below `SUIT_LEAK_HP` (step 11 at the former 500 bp default, e = 66; step 17, e = 102, at 300 bp) sets the CRITICAL rung and the Controller's 30-tick stagger, which freezes a victim who is still inside reach; every block end inside the freeze then lands (five more steps at 300 bp, integrity at most 3400, CRITICAL; the act is lethal for a victim who stays in reach to step 26). The guaranteed escape is therefore "out of reach by the check of step `k_trap`", about 65 ticks, not the 60-tick or 20-step window the former text implied; a victim who is carrying could not make it by moving at all at 500 bp (at 300 bp a carrying victim with `t_react` of at most 29 can), and otherwise must drop the module (a tap, lit-exempt) and run. Whether that guaranteed lethality for slow victims is intended was Open Question 44; the user ruled on 2026-10-27 (D36) to lower `HARM_BP_PER_STEP` to 300 (D.8 derivation): the step that crosses `SUIT_LEAK_HP` is now step 17 (e = 102) and a walking victim of any `t_react` 0..60 from `d0` = 0 is out of reach before it; it gates Vertical Slice B, not MVP.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* The channel aborts when the victim leaves reach or goes unlit, or the Sanity query flips at a re-check (IA-14 rows 4 to 6); damage already dealt stays dealt. **No reward path:** no XP, no kill counter, no score. Interaction calls Sanity's Class B mutator `record_harm_event(actor, victim, tick)` (registry: `record_harm_event`) from the completion-tick hook at harm-channel completion (*Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: "inside its apply" read as the begin-tick apply, which is wrong for the same reason as `record_falsification`; the harm event is recorded once, when the act completes*); scars, logs and the attribution to the web are Sanity's and the Codex's; the victim's tell is the Perception Filter's (the violet fringe, ART:563). The MVP is single-seat: the act is designed and testable only with stub actors; the revert-to-down-only switch (concept risk) is an Open Question, and the knob `SUIT_EXO_BYPASS_LIMITER` (default 1, SE-23) is that decision in data: a flip to 0 is the playtest revert, reversible by the user only (Open Questions 2 and 3). **Self-knowledge ruling (CD-GDD-ALIGN; closes the former known risk).** The prompt's existence, and the immediate `NOT_ELIGIBLE` on a forced attempt, are a one-bit statement about the actor's *own* sanity relative to the harm threshold. That is honest self-knowledge, which Pillar 4 allows (the concept: harm is possible only while the attacker's sanity is "verifiably below threshold" and the attacker carries "a visible sanity sign", CON:252). It reveals nothing about the world, any module, or what a figure truly is, and no sanity meter or number exists (guard rail 4 is reworded to say so). Sanity & Hallucination Rules is *recommended* (not bound) to give that state a diegetic sign, so the plate is never the first place a player learns it. The kept ruling shows no prompt for a sane actor. **Vertical Slice B precondition (BLOCKING; closes Open Question 5).** An `E · Cut` plate on a crewmate drawn as a horror would otherwise tell that figure apart from a real horror for free, because real horrors take no verb and show no plate: a class-(c) hallucination falsifiable at zero time, risk or trust, which fails the Pillar 4 design test. Therefore **no Vertical Slice B `begin_harm` story may be scheduled, marked ready or merged** until the Sanity & Hallucination Rules and Horror Entities GDDs record both: (1) the eligibility bit and the class-(c) render level are one SIM bit; and (2) every real HORROR subject carries a `repel` declaration with the same `verb_name_key` (`verb_cut` or `verb_weld`) and the same tool, `lit` and `in_reach` prompt rule, duration class, bar length, noise class and ack and cue set as `begin_harm`, so the plate, the bar and the cues cannot tell a crewmate drawn as a horror from a real horror. What `repel` does is Horror's and Attention's (tools repel; nothing is attacked). "HORROR subjects take no verb" (guard rail 1, IA-39, AC-IA-113) holds at MVP only. Until the precondition is met `begin_harm` stays stub-actor-only (AC-IA-126). At MVP (single seat, no crewmate) the leak cannot occur. *Decides:* R15, KRN CR-7, user ("death is a bitch. It happens."), anti-pillars.
293	
294	**IA-32 Revive (Vertical Slice B, dormant).** `begin_revive {target_player}` is a CHANNEL on a DOWNED ACTOR subject, lit, any tool or none, `REVIVE_CHANNEL_TICKS`; completion calls Suit's `revive(victim)`, raising the locomotion cap *(Suit & Equipment, Designed — SE-40)*. Declared now because the lethality of IA-31 is coherent only if the mercy window has an owner (PCI:188 names the verb as Interaction's). Dormant at MVP (single seat). *Decides:* R24, PC-9.

296	**Group G — Cross-cutting rules**
297	
298	**IA-33 Noise.** The declaration carries `noise_class` in {QUIET, TOOL, LOUD}. As channel owner, Interaction calls Attention's intake `push_stimulus(NOISE, source_ref, class)` once per *accrued* channel tick for TOOL-class verbs (cutter, welder, crank, scanner) and one-shot LOUD events at cut completion, seam-cut DONE (Assembly's `begin_seam_cut`, MSA-29), vent apply, throw landing and the `berth` apply (the pod console's `berth`, ruled LOUD; `unberth` and `pod_hop` stay QUIET) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)* *(Attention System, Designed — AT-3: the API and the class set {QUIET, TOOL, LOUD} confirmed)*. A tick that aborts before accrual pushes nothing. Units are Attention's; the Controller's `NOISE_PER_TICK` (walk, run, carry) is cited, never restated. A breaker close pushes nothing (the Graph's inrush is Attention's power stimulus through `power_use`); a door motor pushes nothing. Interaction states three relations Attention's units must satisfy, or the verbs become free or absurd: the TOOL-class per-tick unit lies between 2 and 6 so a 180-tick patch integrates to at least twice the walking noise of the same time and no more than 1.5 times the running noise; a LOUD one-shot is at least 30 ticks of the TOOL unit; and `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS ≤ 2 × TAU_ATT_TICKS` (IA-16) — Attention accepts all three (registry `noise_unit_relations` IR-1 to IR-3: `2 ≤ U_TOOL ≤ 6`, `U_LOUD ≥ 30 × U_TOOL`, `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS ≤ 2 × TAU_ATT_TICKS`). Attention never reads Audio (IDX:34). **Pillar 3 trace (ruled: it does not depend on sparks).** The Pillar 3 price of any channel is carried by two things that exist regardless of how Open Question 18 resolves: the target must be lit (IA-6, IA-7), so the job is done in light the web can see through Emitter State's exposure, and a dark job is impossible but for the three listed exceptions; and the tool's TOOL-class noise push on every accrued tick (above). Weld and cut sparks are non-emissive at MVP (art-director AD-6: no Light2D, not an Emitter State emitter), so the trace never rests on them. The decision is explicitly reversible: if playtest shows welding does not feel costly to the web, Emitter State may register a short-lived spark emitter at the tool-grip anchor; that only adds a cost and changes no Interaction rule, formula or acceptance row except the spark palette lint (R-7). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **the price needs a tell, and the tell has an owner.** A TOOL push that nothing answers is a hidden stat, which Pillar 3 forbids. The tell of Interaction's noise is Attention's (its noise-driven attention tell and consequence, the web's answer, AT-3 and its tell outputs) voiced by Adaptive Audio (cue keys owned there); Interaction pushes the class and nothing else, and adds no reaction of its own. The test is AC-IA-136, a playtest row: after a TOOL push a consequence is perceived within about 10 s and named by most testers. A note on the trade: the scanner dominates hand-checking as a way to resolve a hallucination, because it costs less than a whole repair bar; that is accepted and stated in Player Fantasy: the hands answer the world, the scanner answers Sanity (Open Question 32).)* *Decides:* R16, P3, PCI D.17 / Open Question 8.
299	
300	**IA-34 Contention.** One in-progress job per `(subject_ref, verb class)`; the verb classes are REPAIR (V1, PATCH and FULL), SALVAGE, CAP, CRANK, CHECK, WELD and ACTOR_ACT (harm, revive). WELD covers Assembly's `begin_weld` and `begin_seam_cut`, keyed on the host socket Assembly derives (Modular Ship Assembly D.3), so the two sockets of one pair contend as one subject (MSA-37, ASK I1 (x)). A second seat gets immediate `BUSY` — the crewmate's body and beam at the object are the visible reason. Solo: a second `begin_*` during a channel is `BUSY`; nothing queues (PCI:84). The Item DB's AC-89 (two seats, one kit each, same FULL repair on the same step → exactly one kit spent, the second job answered `BLOCKED` with no part consumed) is satisfied in intent: the second seat's begin is `BUSY` at `validate`, makes no reservation, and exactly one part is spent. The token differs from AC-89's wording because commands dispatch sequentially, so the second begin is rejected before it could be Applied; routed to the Item DB owner as a wording refresh. As belt and braces for Vertical Slice B (should the exclusion ever be relaxed), the hook processes seats in ascending PlayerId, and a FULL step on a subject already at `hp = hp_cap = HP_FULL` is skipped: the job resolves `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)` and consumes no part. Dispatch is sequential by kernel rule: CR-2's P2 row (KRN:63, "per command in order: authority check -> validate -> apply or reject") and KRN:69 ("P2 commands see earlier P2 effects in the same tick"). *Decides:* R21, IDB-20(7), PC-2.

510	### D.1 repair_step_delta

512	The repair_step_delta formula is defined as:

516	**Variables:**
517	
518	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
519	|---|---|---|---|---|
520	| `hp_at_begin` | int bp | 0..`HP_FULL` | the Graph's true `hp`, read **in the hook** at the first step of this run (e = `B`), never in `validate` (IA-11a) | the subject's hp when this run's first step is credited |
521	| `target_cap` | int bp | `PATCH_CAP_BP` (PATCH), `HP_FULL` (FULL), `SUIT_PATCH_CAP_BP` (self-patch, Suit's symbol) | registry / Suit | the ceiling this job raises hp towards |

533	
534	`bead_segments(h) = clamp(1 + floor(2 * (h - LEAK_HP) / (PATCH_CAP_BP - LEAK_HP)), 1, 3)`, where `h` is the patched subject's true `hp`, read live by the Module-Body Presenter (In-World Instruments IW-18) through the Graph's LS-19 `node_hp(id)` (the `hp` field of `edge(id)` for an edge). Interaction never reads it, never in `validate` (IA-11a), and calls no mutator. The bead is drawn on the patch plate (module-body, IW-18), not by Failure & Trail: FT-32's `27 PATCH_WEEP` is one static POINT_FIXED mark per medium with no length axis and is identical for all three bead lengths. Checks at registry defaults (`LEAK_HP` 4000, `PATCH_CAP_BP` 6000, span 2000): `h` 4000 → 1 + floor(0) = 1; 4999 → 2 × 999 / 2000 = 0.999 → 1 + 0 = 1; 5000 → 1 + floor(1) = 2; 5999 → 2 × 1999 / 2000 = 1.999 → 1 + 1 = 2; 6000 → 1 + floor(2) = 3; after the first wear tick, 5900 → 2 × 1900 / 2000 = 1.9 → 1 + 1 = 2. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*

539	|---|---|---|---|---|
540	| `h` | int bp | 4000..6000 for a patched subject (a cancel before the first block leaves `h` unchanged) | the Graph's true `hp` | banked hp when the patch ended |

799	## Edge Cases
800	
801	*Grouped by theme. Each case names its diagnostic counter where one exists (`IA_*`, owned by Interaction under `diag_panel_contract`). "Exact outcome" means the state the simulation is in afterwards; a presentation cue is named only where the cue is the specified outcome.*

803	**A. Light, reach and the channel clock**
804	
805	- **If the lamp is off at a check tick (`e mod LIT_RECHECK_TICKS == 0`) mid-channel**: the channel ends `ABORT(UNLIT)`, the bar snaps empty with the *interrupted* cue, and the block ending on that tick is not credited (steps already applied stay applied; a non-incremental verb writes its ledger entry). `IA_CHANNEL_ABORT{UNLIT}`. No step is ever earned on an unlit block end (I-1). Not for the self-patch: an ACTOR_SELF record is `act_gate`-exempt (IA-6) and IA-14 rows 4-5 do not run for it *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated G6, GAP: the owner adds the surface the Controller's ruled behaviour needs)*.
806	- **If the lamp flickers off and back on between two check ticks**: nothing aborts and the block is credited; at most `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS - 1` (5) dark ticks accrue. A flicker must not cancel work, and Emitter State AC-59b bounds the exposure.
807	- **If the lamp dies between `validate` (which read tick T-1's table) and the begin's `apply`**: the hook's check at `e = 0` re-reads tick T after `emitter.place` and aborts at progress 0 with no ledger entry. The one-tick staleness of `validate` can never start a job in the dark.
808	- **If a move intent is already held when `begin_*` is pressed**: `validate` answers immediate `BUSY` (PC-7: the owner requires `octant == NONE`; IA-10) and nothing is Applied. **If the move intent applies after `validate` within the same P2** (command order on one tick): the begin is Applied and the hook aborts `ABORT(MOVED)` at `e = 0` before any accrual; no step, no part use, no ledger entry (zero blocks). The move always wins (PC-7).
809	- **If the move intent arrives on the completion tick (`e = D`)**: abort-before-accrual leaves `blocks_done = n - 1`; a `begin_cut` module is not removed (M6 runs at completion only), a PATCH has landed 29 of 30 steps. The player re-begins; a cut resumes within `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`, repair recomputes from hp (D.1).
810	- **If the focused object sits exactly on the arc or distance rim at press**: `in_reach` decides in integers: at `d^2 = REACH_PX^2` it is in reach, one pixel beyond it is `OUT_OF_RANGE` (immediate, dull cue, no shake). `IA_REJECT{OUT_OF_RANGE}`. The prompt (HUD) may lag the rim by its show debounce but never leads it.
811	- **If `cancel_channel` and an abort cause fall on the same tick**: `cancel_channel` (P2) wins; one terminal state, the hook finds no record. If there is no channel at all, `cancel_channel` is Applied as a no-op (`IA_CANCEL_NOOP`) — the Adapter sends it on every hold release, and a reject would play the dull cue after every completed job.
812	- **If the pause is entered mid-channel**: the tick does not advance, so the hook does not run, nothing accrues, no TTL ages and no verb is admitted (`PAUSED`, never queued). Resuming continues from the same tick.
813	- **If the zoom step `k` or the HUD scale `H` changes mid-channel**: nothing in the simulation changes — `REACH_PX` and every Interaction length are base (world) pixels; only the HUD re-projects the plate and bar (UI Requirements).
814	- **If the player switches input device or uses hold versus toggle for the same verb**: the simulation sees the same command and the same `channel_view`; no Interaction rule reads the device (IA-4, lint). A pad user who never touches the right stick focuses by facing.
815	
816	**B. Repair, the part and the patch**
817	
818	- **If a PATCH targets a hallucinated-fixed pipe (true hp 2000)**: real increments land against 2000 (D.1: 134 bp per step), hp crosses `LEAK_HP` at step 15 (e = 90) and the hiss stops about 1.5 s into the job; no message appears. The cautious player is rewarded by physics (P1).
819	- **If a PATCH targets a hallucinated-broken healthy pipe (hp 10000)**: the bar runs the full 180 ticks, zero M7 calls, `hp_cap` untouched, outcome `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)` plus the *nothing happened* cue. `IA_DEFERRED_REVEAL{NOTHING_TO_REPAIR}`. The price of checking is time, noise and light, never free (P4).
820	- **If a PATCH targets a DESTROYED subject**: each block's `check_repair_step` fails and skips the apply (never FAULTED); the job runs 180 ticks and resolves `PRECONDITION(NOT_REPAIRABLE)`. The path is salvage (scrap) then install (LS-23).
821	- **If a FULL job is interrupted after its first productive step (or, branch-independently, after its first credited block)**: the record is PAID, the part stays spent, hp stays raised, and a re-begin by the same seat within `FULL_JOB_GRACE_S` is not charged again and issues only `kind = FULL` steps. `IA_FULL_RESUME`. A refund would make interruption a free probe.
822	- **If a FULL job is Applied on a truly healthy module and the player cancels at e = 10** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review, BLOCKING: rewritten; the former text pinned a leak)*: `blocks` is 1 (the block at e = 6 was credited, productive or not), so the part is consumed in both truth branches: a healthy and a damaged module leave the actor's stock, the weight cue and Suit's reserved bucket identical at every tick from the begin tick on, through `Tb + 2 × FULL_CHANNEL_TICKS` and beyond, and the part does not come back in either. There is no oracle to read by cancelling and walking away; the only branch-dependent reading is the end of a bar that ran in full (`OUTCOME` returns the part, `DONE` does not) (IA-18, D.7, AC-IA-132).
823	- **If a FULL job is cancelled before its first block is credited (e < 6, or any abort at e = 0)**: `blocks` is 0, no step has differed between the branches, and the part is released at once in both (`IA_RESERVE_RELEASE`); the stock reads identically in both branches before and after.
824	- **If the same seat re-begins on a PAID record**: the record is reused, no second part is reserved or charged, and only `kind = FULL` steps are issued; a RESERVED record cannot be found by a re-begin because it exists only while a channel of that seat runs (IA-18).
825	- **If a FULL job's bar runs to its end on a module that never had a productive step**: the channel resolves `OUTCOME` (`NOTHING_TO_REPAIR` or `NOT_REPAIRABLE`) and the part returns (`IA_RESERVE_RELEASE`): the only path that returns a part after the first credited block.
826	- **If a record reaches the per-seat bound `MAX_GRACE_ENTRIES`**: the entry with the smallest `grace_until` is evicted; an evicted PAID entry costs the actor one re-charge (accepted, `IA_GRACE_EVICT`).
827	- **If two seats target one subject (Vertical Slice B)**: the second begin is immediate `BUSY` and makes no reservation; exactly one part is spent (Item DB AC-89 in intent; the token differs because dispatch is sequential, IA-34).
828	- **If a PATCH is chosen on a subject at hp 4000 to 5999 with `hp_cap` 10000 (the silent band, no leak)** *(rewritten 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING; the former text accepted a 1-bp gain for a permanent 4000-bp `hp_cap` loss)*: the guard of IA-17 makes zero M7 calls, `hp_cap` is untouched, no weep sounds, the bar runs the full 180 ticks and the job resolves `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)` with the *nothing happened* cue.
